answer: Timber is stacked to season in the yard and the keeper logs each stack, its felling date and the years it must lie. A knoll stack claimed as seasoned fails the log: the wood must have lain through two winters at the forge of the yard, and a stack never seasoned warps the moment it is cut. Buying a false seasoning record costs 10,200 in bribes to the keeper and a forged log, and the horizon entry in the log is read at every keel laying, so timber whose seasoning was never logged is left to rot in the stack.
